text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty page fired — GPU_MEM_PRESSURE on pool-gamma (node: gnode-17). PD link: https://pd.redwood.example/incidents/PD-4951236789. Reason: nvml/cuda alloc failures spike. Auto-suppress: false.

pagerduty: Assigned to josh.s — auto-page acknowledged. Escalation policy: platform-lead after 5m sustained OOM.

josh.s: Ack — I'm oncall. Pulling logs and metrics now.

maria.k: Seeing repeated 'CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY' and 'NVRM: Xid' driver resets in /var/log/kern.log starting ~02:12UTC. KV-cache evictions spiking on pool-gamma.

josh.s: Quick check — impact? any 5xx spikes for external customers?

maria.k: Host metrics show 502/504 errors up ~0.8% overall for pool-gamma in last 5m. Tenants flagged: tenant-alpha, tenant-beta. Hosted customers unaffected (different pool).

alex.p: Can we reroute traffic from pool-gamma to pool-beta and enable fallback to quantized-v1 for latency-sensitive routes? Pool-beta has ~30% spare capacity.

josh.s: Yes. Immediate plan: 1) cordon + drain gnode-17, 2) update routing policy to avoid pool-gamma for new requests, 3) enable quantized fallback for model-small routes, 4) capture NVML dump + logs, 5) create incident ticket.

josh.s: ```
kubectl cordon gnode-17
kubectl drain gnode-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=300s
```

ops-runner: Drain started — evicting 6 pods (serving: model-small replicas). Pod bounce in progress. Watch: https://k8s.redwood.example/nodes/gnode-17

maria.k: Pushed a temporary kvcache parameter change on the node to reduce prefetch (ops-runbook kvcache/tune): `/ops/kvcache set --node gnode-17 --target-evict=0.65` — this should lower memory pressure while we move traffic.

josh.s: Routing update applied: route-policy:model-small now prefers pool-beta region:us-west-2. New sessions are routing away. Reverting will be manual.

pagerduty: Escalation executed per runbook — notifying platform lead (alex.p).

alex.p: Oncall here. Confirming driver resets in kernel logs? Maria, can you capture NVML state and GPU diagnostics before we reprovision?

maria.k: Running nvml-dump now: `/opt/tools/nvml-dump --node gnode-17 > /tmp/nvml-gnode-17.log` — will upload after finished. Also grabbing dmesg and serving logs.

josh.s: Uploaded artifacts to S3: s3://redwood-ops/incidents/4951236789/ (nvml-dump.log, kern-dmesg.log, serving-gpu.log).

maria.k: After routing change and draining, error rate dropped to ~0.2% within 4m. Latency tail improving. No new OOMs observed on pool-beta.

josh.s: Decision: decommission gnode-17 for forensic (reimage/drivers). Opening incident ticket INC-4951236789 with Sev=2. Notifying account managers for tenant-alpha and tenant-beta.

alex.p: Agreed — we will isolate node, escalate to infra-driver team to check for driver-level leak (attach nvml logs). Add follow-up: check kernel module versions and recent driver rollouts.

ops-runner: Node cordoned and drained successfully. All pods moved off gnode-17. Node marked unschedulable.

josh.s: I've left a note in PD: https://pd.redwood.example/incidents/PD-4951236789 — marking on-call handoff window; I'll be primary until 03:00UTC then hand to nightshift.

maria.k: Monitoring for 15m. Will post metrics link and initial timeline to the ticket.

josh.s: Thanks — creating a short action list in the ticket: capture dumps (done), driver team triage, account ping, postmortem within 72h. If error rate goes above 1% again, re-open PD.

incident-bot: PD incident updated: status=mitigated, auto-close timer paused for follow-up.

josh.s: Closing Slack thread for immediate mitigation. Will update ticket with root-cause hypothesis after driver team analysis. Followup: postmortem and rollout checklist. :white_check_mark:
